java.say: `new PdfReport()` makes a PdfReport object. The variable `report` has the type Report, the general kind. That works because PdfReport extends Report: a PdfReport is a Report.
The program asks the report to make itself. It does not say how.

PdfReport has no generate() of its own, so it uses the one from its parent class Report. This method is the template: it lists the steps in a fixed order. `final` means that no subclass may change this list.
Step 1: fetch the data. In Report this step is `abstract`: it has a name but no code. Each subclass must write its own version.
Java looks at the real object, a PdfReport, and runs the PdfReport version of the step.
Step 2: lay out the report. Again, Report only gives the step a name.
This step does have code in Report, and PdfReport does not replace it. So the shared version runs: every report gets the same footer.
All three steps are done, so generate() ends. Report decided the order; PdfReport only filled in the blanks.
Back in the program. With `new HtmlReport()` on the first line, the same three steps run in the same order, but steps 1 and 2 come from HtmlReport.
